column1: # tests/fixtures/pr-slug/cases.tsv - the executable statement of the PR-slug
# contract: what "<owner>" and "<repo>" a GitHub PR url or a clone remote names.
# section 7 makes it the owner of the "+captain-merge" merge-policy decision), so
# the "owner"/"repo" columns are AUTHORITATIVE: a change that moves them is a
# change to a permission path, not a refactor.
# The logbook connector re-implements the same parse out of tree
# connector/firstmate/lb-fm-compose.sh project_remote_repo for the remote half),
# where it decides whether that repo's Merge control may be offered. The "peer"
# columns record what THAT side produces today, so a disagreement is written down
# rather than discovered when a forbidden merge slips through. Reconciling them
# is the logbook side's work; this file is what it reconciles against.
# TAB-separated. "#" starts a comment line. Fields:
#   input       the url or remote to parse
#   peer_owner  the peer's owner ("=" when peer is agree)
#   peer_repo   the peer's repo  ("=" when peer is agree)
#   note        why the case is here
# "~" is the empty string in any field. An empty owner or repo is a DELIBERATE
# answer, not a parse failure: half a name identifies nothing, so the pair is
# unmatchable and the merge is permitted on this signal alone.

column8: note

column1: # --- the ordinary shapes both sides read alike -------------------------------

column8: the canonical PR url
a zero-padded PR number is still numeric
the scheme is not part of the slug
case is preserved here and folded by fm_merge_same_part
only the two components above /pull/ are read
an owner-less path reads the host as the owner and so matches no clone
a non-numeric PR number is not a PR url
a missing PR number is not a PR url
a query string is not one of the two tolerated suffixes
a fragment is not one of the two tolerated suffixes
a sub-path is not one of the two tolerated suffixes
exactly ONE trailing slash is tolerated, no more
no owner and no repo to read
the empty input resolves to nothing

column1: # --- DECLARED divergences on the url half ------------------------------------
# Each of these is a url firstmate resolves and the connector does not, or
# resolves differently. Firstmate's answer is the authoritative one, and its
# extra width is deliberate: a url the guard cannot resolve is a merge it cannot
# trace back to a flagged clone, so narrowing this side to the peer's reopens the
# bypass. Asserting the peer's value here means a later narrowing fails the suite.

column8: one trailing slash is tolerated here and rejected by the connector
a .git repo component is normalized here so the url and the clone origin resolve alike
both tolerances at once
fm_merge_slug reads any non-PR string as a REMOTE; the connector's is url-only. Harmless: no clone origin resolves to "pulls/7"
same dual-purpose fall-through; bin/fm-pr-merge.sh refuses a non-GitHub provider before the guard is consulted

column1: # --- DECLARED divergences that are mechanical, not behavioural ---------------
# fm_merge_slug blanks a whitespace-bearing half on BOTH sides; the connector
# blanks it on the remote side only. Both therefore match nothing either way, so
# no merge decision turns on the difference - but the halves differ, so they are
# written down rather than left to look like an agreement.

column8: whitespace cannot appear in a GitHub repo name; blanking it keeps the pair unmatchable
the same on the owner half

a trailing slash
the scp-style form leaves "host:" on the owner
the scp-style form without .git
an owner-less scp remote yields no owner and so matches no PR url
the ssh:// form
case is preserved and folded at comparison time
a path remote reads like any other
both sides blank a whitespace-bearing repo here
a clone with no origin claims nothing

column8: ORDER IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE: the trailing slash comes off before the .git behind it. What "git clone https://github.com/acme/guarded.git/" records verbatim, and the peer's answer matches no PR url, so that clone claims nothing and its merge is permitted
a doubled suffix defeats BOTH single-pass strips; recorded, not fixed, because neither answer matches a PR url and no real origin has this shape
